Senses.Explanation: Literally, purple (紫) fungus (芝). Dafang Xinghai's mountain verse is the corpus's direct plant action: he is too indolent to gather purple fungus beside the stream (懶去溪邊採紫芝). The plant-name circulates much more widely in the compound Purple Fungus Song. Tiantong Shanxin is publicly asked what that song is and answers by clapping; Fahua Quanju answers an independent transmission of the question by saying that it is not a Wu sound but must be Han speech (不是吳音，切湏漢語). Yongjue Yuanxian asks who will join a solitary recluse in singing it (中有幽人守貞獨，誰來同唱紫芝歌), Xisou Shaotan places groups of two and three singing it on stones under pine roots (三三兩兩松根石上唱紫芝歌), and Yuanwu Keqin asks who can sing it in the season of high mountains, autumn wind, and a single goose (誰當此時節，解唱紫芝歌). Wuwen Daocan separately invokes the Four Hoaryheads of Mount Shang and their heart of withdrawal, but his verse does not contain the headword. Zen bends the plant-name into a song asked about in public interviews and sung in mountain-retreat verse. The evidence does not make the bare word itself the title of a second thing.
Senses.Note: The unsplit string has 136 hits in 72 allowlisted texts, including collisions with personal and place names. Purple Fungus Song (紫芝歌) has 20 hits in 18 texts; gathering purple fungus (採紫芝) occurs once. Six exact witnesses cover plant action, two distinct public answers, solitary and communal singing, and Yuanwu's seasonal verse; one marked family witness preserves the requested Four-Hoaryheads comparison. Purple-Fungus Hermitage and Purple-Fungus Crag are place compounds rather than lexical senses. The lineage-title and person uses are separated into the following sense rather than collapsed into the plant.

Senses.Explanation: The same graphs also occur as a Chan title and person-name. The Chan Lamp of the Jin River heads a biography “Chan Master Zizhi Zang” (紫芝藏禪師), says that he was born to the Zhang family in Ba County (巴縣張氏子), shaved his head at Great Emei, attended Lingfa Chang for years, received his approval, and later opened the teaching at Zhulin Hall. The Complete Collection of the Five Lamps independently transmits the same Ba-County, Great-Emei, Lingfa-Chang, and Zhulin biography. The Jin River record then marks “lineage heirs of Zizhi Zang” (紫芝藏法嗣). Within that lineage section, Qiongmu Wen's biography says that he heard Zizhi opening the hall, went to meet him, served in the attendant quarters for fifteen years, and was approved (聞紫芝和尚開堂，杖笠往參，充侍寮十五年，遂印可焉). The Recorded Sayings of Zhulangsheng of Qingcheng separately records a direct encounter at Wannian Temple on Emei: Zhulangsheng meets the recorded Chan figure Zizhi (遇紫芝禪師), and the two exchange remarks about Hongchunping, rain pressing on the towers, and leeches along the road. The shared Sichuan and Emei setting makes identification with Zizhi Zang plausible, but that encounter does not supply the name Zang or a lineage statement, so this entry does not declare the identification certain. Zen deployment here is biographical and lineage-bearing: Zizhi opens the hall, approves Qiongmu Wen, has named lineage heirs, and speaks in a recorded encounter.
Senses.Note: This is a proper-name and title sense, distinct from the fungus. The headed biographies securely identify Zizhi Zang; the Qiongmu Wen passage is filed under his lineage heirs. The Emei encounter names only Chan Master Zizhi, so its identity with Zizhi Zang remains probable rather than certain. Different references to a person or title do not create separate lexical senses merely because the record may leave the individual's full name unresolved.

Occurrences.Kwic: 紫芝藏禪師紫芝藏禪師巴縣張氏子。自髫披剃于大峩，參靈筏和尚巾瓶有年，一日印可，後開法于竹林堂。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Chan Lamp of the Jin River (錦江禪燈), headed biography of Zizhi Zang. It names Zizhi Zang, his Ba-County Zhang family, ordination at Great Emei, attendance on Lingfa Chang, approval, and later opening of the teaching at Zhulin Hall. Zizhi Zang is not yet in the roster; the source-attested name supplies the provisional pinyin form.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Collection of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), supplementary biography of Zizhi Zang. The compilation independently transmits the Ba-County, Great-Emei, Lingfa-Chang, approval, and Zhulin details.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Chan Lamp of the Jin River (錦江禪燈). The lineage heading explicitly introduces the lineage heirs of Zizhi Zang; the duplicated normalized wording comes from the table-of-contents and section heading at the same location.

Occurrences.Kwic: 聞紫芝和尚開堂，杖笠往參，充侍寮十五年，遂印可焉。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Chan Lamp of the Jin River (錦江禪燈), biography of Qiongmu Wen within the lineage-heirs section of Zizhi Zang. It says that Qiongmu heard Zizhi open the hall, went to meet him, served in the attendant quarters for fifteen years, and received approval.

Occurrences.Kwic: 宿萬年寺，遇紫芝禪師，問：『曾到洪樁坪否？』予曰：『一天煙雨壓樓臺。』紫曰：『好則好，秖是沿路螞蟥多。』
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhulangsheng of Qingcheng (青城竹浪生禪師語錄). At Wannian Temple on Emei, Zhulangsheng meets a Chan master called Zizhi; Zizhi asks about Hongchunping and responds to Zhulangsheng's rain-and-towers line by mentioning the many leeches along the road. The passage does not give Zizhi's fuller name, so the provisional speaker name is Zizhi rather than a certain identification with Zizhi Zang.
